purpose: Sense-level corrections for existing English baseline entries; apply by exact normalized headword during consolidated integration.
status: editorially-authored; awaiting full review and integration

senses.definition: The ability, right or opportunity to enter, use or obtain something.
senses.definitionZh: 使用权；访问权；进入机会
examples: Students have access to the library after class.
The new ramp gives wheelchair users easier access to the building.

senses.definition: To enter, open or retrieve information or a place, especially by using a computer or account.
examples: I cannot access my account because I forgot the password.
You can access the lesson materials from your profile.

senses.definition: A way or method of dealing with a task, problem or situation.
examples: We need a different approach to this problem.
The team discussed a more practical approach to the project.

senses.definition: To move closer to someone or something, or to speak to someone in order to ask or offer something.
examples: A stranger approached me to ask for directions.
She approached the manager about changing her schedule.

senses.definition: An effort to do something, especially something difficult or uncertain.
examples: I made another attempt to solve the puzzle.
Her first attempt was unsuccessful, but she tried again.

senses.definition: To try to do or achieve something, especially when it may be difficult.
examples: She attempted to explain the issue calmly.
Do not attempt to repair the device while it is connected to power.

senses.definition: A condition in which different parts are equal or in the correct proportions; also the amount of money remaining in an account.
examples: It can be difficult to maintain a balance between work and rest.
Please check the balance in your account before making a payment.

senses.definition: To keep something steady or to arrange different activities or needs in suitable proportions.
examples: She balanced the box carefully on the shelf.
He tries to balance his studies with a part-time job.

senses.definition: An advantage, helpful result or positive effect.
examples: One benefit of walking is better fitness.
The main benefit of the update is faster search.

senses.definition: To be helped or improved by something.
examples: You'll benefit from getting enough sleep.
Small businesses can benefit from the new support programme.

senses.definition: A difficult task or situation that tests someone's ability, skill or determination.
examples: Learning pronunciation is a challenge for me.
Finding enough time to study can be a challenge.

senses.definition: To question whether something is correct or to test someone's ability or confidence.
examples: The project challenged us to think creatively.
The lawyer challenged the accuracy of the report.

senses.definition: Having all the necessary parts, details or elements; whole and finished.
examples: The project is complete, so we can relax.
Please send the complete list of participants.

senses.definition: To finish doing or making something.
examples: Please complete the form before Friday.
She completed the course in three months.

senses.definition: A period of waiting or a situation in which something happens later than expected.
examples: There was a delay because of heavy rain.
The flight arrived with a two-hour delay.

senses.definition: To make something happen later than planned or to wait before doing something.
examples: The technician delayed the appointment until Monday.
We decided to delay the launch until the tests were complete.

senses.definition: A small piece of information or a particular feature of something.
examples: Please check every detail before submitting.
The report includes details about the new schedule.

senses.definition: To describe or explain something fully and carefully.
examples: He detailed the steps in his report.
The guide details how to set up the account.

senses.definition: Training, self-control or rules that help people behave properly or work towards a goal; also an area of study.
examples: Daily practice takes discipline.
Biology is one of the subjects in her academic discipline.

senses.definition: To train or correct someone, especially by using rules or consequences.
examples: The school disciplined the student for repeatedly breaking the rules.
She disciplined herself to stop checking her phone while studying.

senses.definition: An early version of a piece of writing, plan or design that may be changed later.
examples: I finished the first draft of my cover letter.
The designer showed the client a draft of the new poster.

senses.definition: To prepare an early version of a document, plan or message.
examples: Can you draft a short introduction?
The committee drafted a proposal for the new course.

senses.definition: Knowledge or skill gained by doing something; or an event that happens to someone.
examples: Work experience can help you find a job.
The trip was a memorable experience for the whole family.

senses.definition: To go through or feel an event, change or condition.
examples: I experienced a lot of growth this year.
Many people experience stress before an important interview.

senses.definition: Reasonable, just and treating people equally; also moderately good or acceptable.
examples: I think that is a fair price.
The teacher gave everyone a fair chance.

senses.definition: A public event where people meet for entertainment or where goods, services or information are displayed and sold.
examples: We visited the book fair at the convention centre.
The town holds a food fair every autumn.

senses.definition: The main centre of attention, interest or activity.
examples: My main focus is improving my English.
Safety should remain the focus of the discussion.

senses.definition: To give attention to one particular person, subject or activity.
examples: Let us focus on the most important task.
The camera focused on the subject in the foreground.

senses.definition: A strong effect or influence that one thing has on another; also the force of one object hitting another.
examples: The change had a positive impact on the team.
The impact of the collision damaged the front of the car.

senses.definition: To have a strong effect on someone or something.
examples: Small habits can impact your progress.
The new rules may impact local businesses.

senses.definition: To become greater in amount, size, number or degree, or to make something greater.
examples: The price may increase next month.
The company plans to increase production this year.

senses.definition: A rise in amount, size, number or degree.
examples: We saw an increase in visitors.
There has been a small increase in the cost of materials.

senses.definition: A feeling of wanting to know or learn about something; also an advantage or right connected with something.
examples: I have a strong interest in animation.
The agreement protects the interests of both groups.

senses.definition: To make someone curious or want to know more about something.
examples: This topic interests me.
The museum's new exhibition may interest younger visitors.

senses.definition: An important subject for discussion, or a problem that needs attention.
examples: We need to solve this issue quickly.
The meeting focused on the issue of public safety.

senses.definition: To officially give, publish or send something, such as a document, statement or instruction.
examples: The office issued a new access card.
The school issued a notice about the holiday schedule.

senses.definition: To see, hear or become aware of someone or something.
examples: Did you notice the sign near the door?
I noticed that she looked tired.

senses.definition: A written or spoken announcement that gives information or a warning.
examples: A notice was posted beside the entrance.
The landlord gave us one month's notice before the repair work.

senses.definition: A particular idea, fact or detail; or a score in a game or competition.
examples: The main point is to keep the message clear.
Our team scored the winning point in the final minute.

senses.definition: To direct a finger, hand or object towards someone or something.
examples: He pointed toward the exit when the alarm sounded.
She pointed at the detail she wanted me to notice.

senses.definition: Repeated activity used to improve a skill; or the usual way of doing something.
examples: Daily practice helps build confidence.
It is common practice to back up important files.

senses.definition: To do an activity repeatedly in order to improve at it or become familiar with it.
examples: I practice speaking English with a friend.
The team practised the presentation before the event.

senses.definition: Words or actions that express approval, admiration or respect.
examples: He received praise for helping the new staff.
The teacher's praise encouraged the student to keep trying.

senses.definition: To express approval or admiration for someone or something.
examples: The manager praised her careful work.
Critics praised the film for its strong performances.

senses.definition: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular result.
examples: Learning is a gradual process.
The application process takes about two weeks.

senses.definition: To deal with information, materials or a request by carrying out a series of operations.
examples: Give me a moment to process the information.
The office processes applications in the order they arrive.

senses.definition: Movement or development towards a goal or a better condition.
examples: You have made good progress this month.
The project is making steady progress.

senses.definition: To develop, improve or move forward over time.
examples: The work is progressing more quickly now.
Students progress at different speeds.

senses.definition: To let someone or something go free, or to allow something to leave a container or space.
examples: She released his hand and stepped away.
The valve releases pressure from the system.

senses.definition: The act of making something available, or the act of freeing someone or something.
examples: The software release is scheduled for next week.
The release of the rescued animals was shown on television.

senses.definition: To fix something that is broken, damaged or not working properly.
examples: The technician repaired the laptop.
They repaired the fence after the storm.

senses.definition: The act of fixing something, or the condition of being fixed.
examples: The repair took longer than expected.
The phone is in need of repair.

senses.definition: Something that happens or exists because of an action, event or situation.
examples: The result was better than we expected.
The test results will be available tomorrow.

senses.definition: To happen because of something; usually used with “in” or “from”.
examples: Small daily habits can result in steady progress.
The delay resulted from a technical problem.

senses.definition: The possibility that something harmful, unpleasant or unwanted may happen.
examples: There is a risk of losing unsaved work.
The report explains the risks of driving in heavy rain.

senses.definition: To do something that may expose someone or something to danger, loss or an unwanted result.
examples: Do not risk your safety for a shortcut.
She risked missing the train by leaving too late.

senses.definition: A plan that lists the times when events, activities or tasks are expected to happen.
examples: My schedule is full this week.
The train schedule is available online.

senses.definition: To arrange for an event or task to happen at a particular time.
examples: We scheduled the interview for Monday.
The repair has been scheduled for next week.

senses.definition: Protected from danger, loss or unauthorised access; or firmly fixed in place.
examples: Use a secure password for your account.
Make sure the ladder is secure before climbing.

senses.definition: To obtain or achieve something, often after effort; or to fasten something firmly.
examples: We secured permission to use the room.
Please secure the box with strong tape.
